stem: With reference to India, the terms 'Halbi, Ho and Kui' Pertain to :
expl: Halbi, Ho and Kui are the languages of the tribes. The Halbi language is mainly spoken in Bastar, Chhattisgarh, its speakers are the Rajmuria, Halba, Mahar, Parja, and Lohra tribes, which spread from Odisha to Maharashtra. Ho is the language of the Munda and family, which is spoken by tribes like Ho, Munda and Koi etc. Its main area is West Singhbhum, Jharkhand, while the speakers spread from Odisha to Maharashtra. Kui is a language of the Dravidian family. It is mainly spoken by the Kui tribe in Kandhamal, Odisha.

stem: Which Indian language, is spoken the most in the world after Hindi?
expl: According to Ethnologue 2025, Bengali is the most spoken Indian language in the world after Hindi among the given options. There are a total of 284.3 million users of the Bengali language globally.

stem: Which one of the following is the largest linguistic group of India?
expl: The largest linguistic group in India is Indo-Aryan. This is the most important family of Indian languages and comprises of all the principal languages, including Hindi, Bengali, Gujarati, Marathi, Punjabi, Sindhi, Rajasthani, Assamese, Odiya, Kashmiri, Urdu, and Sanskrit.

stem: Which one of the following languages belongs to the Austric group?
expl: The languages of Austric group (Austro-Asiatic) are Khasi, Santhali, Mundari and Bhumij etc. It is a language spoken by the Indian tribes.

stem: Consider the map given below : The predominant languages spoken in the areas marked A, B, C and D are respectively :
expl: In the area marked as ‘A’, Brajbhasha is spoken. In the area marked ‘B’, Awadhi is spoken. In the area marked ‘C’ Bhojpuri is spoken, and in the area marked as ‘D’, Maithili is spoken, which is the area of North Bihar.

stem: Which of the following was given the classical language status in 2014?
expl: Odiya became the sixth language of the country to get classical language status on 20 Feb, 2014. Classical language status was given to Tamil in 2004, Sanskrit in 2005, Telugu and Kannada in 2008 and Malayalam in 2013.
